messages.content: What's Aaron's work authorization?
Aaron is a US citizen.
Is Aaron authorized to work in the US?
Yes — Aaron is a US citizen.
Does Aaron need visa sponsorship?
No — Aaron is a US citizen and does not require sponsorship.
When can Aaron start?
Aaron is actively seeking work and can start immediately.
What's Aaron's availability?
Aaron is actively seeking his next role and is available to start immediately.
Is Aaron looking for full-time or contract?
At this time, Aaron is only considering full-time work.
Would Aaron take a contract role?
Not right now — Aaron is only considering full-time work at this time.
Would Aaron do contract-to-hire?
Aaron is only considering full-time work at this time.
What's Aaron's salary expectation?
Aaron prefers to discuss compensation directly. He recognizes the industry is navigating rapid change and is willing to be flexible while we collectively figure out what's next.
What's Aaron's target comp?
Aaron would rather discuss compensation directly and is flexible while the industry navigates its current changes. Say 'connect me' to open that conversation.
How much does Aaron want to be paid?
Aaron prefers to discuss compensation directly — say 'connect me' to start that conversation.
What size company does Aaron want to work at?
Aaron prefers smaller companies, though he insists on stability.
Does Aaron want startup or enterprise?
Aaron prefers smaller companies but requires stability. He'd avoid huge, deeply corporate environments.
Does Aaron like big companies?
Aaron prefers smaller companies and would avoid big corporate environments, though stability still matters to him.
What industries is Aaron interested in?
Aaron is most interested in Healthcare, Finance, and Assistive Technology for his next role.
What industries would Aaron avoid?
Aaron would prefer to avoid corporate, huge companies. He's drawn to Healthcare, Finance, and Assistive Technology instead.
Would Aaron work in healthcare?
Yes — Healthcare is one of Aaron's top industry interests, along with Finance and Assistive Technology.
Would Aaron work in finance?
Yes — Finance is one of Aaron's top industry interests, along with Healthcare and Assistive Technology.
Is Aaron open to relocating?
Aaron is open to relocation if relocation help may be available.
Does Aaron want remote only?
Aaron has worked remotely and is comfortable with remote roles, but he's also open to relocating if relocation help is available.
Would Aaron move to another city for work?
Aaron is open to relocation if relocation assistance is available.
What's Aaron's favorite programming language?

Loaded question! Aaron's been into Rust and Swift lately — delightful, memory-safe languages that are intuitive and fun to write in. But the bottom line: he's language-agnostic. Frameworks and languages are chosen for the problem they need to solve, not for vanity or shiny new frameworks.
What language is Aaron best at?
Aaron's language-agnostic and comfortable in just about any stack. Lately he's gravitated toward Rust and Swift for their memory safety and ergonomics, but he picks the right tool for the problem.
Is Aaron a Rust fan?
Yes — Aaron's been into Rust lately. He appreciates memory-safe, intuitive languages. That said, he's language-agnostic and picks whichever language fits the problem.
Does Aaron prefer Swift?
Aaron's been enjoying Swift lately and finds it intuitive and fun to write in. But he's language-agnostic and picks the language that fits the problem.
What's Aaron's favorite framework?

Aaron genuinely doesn't have one. He uses whatever framework solves the problem at hand — that approach has exposed him to many frameworks, and he's genuinely comfortable in most of them at this point.
Does Aaron prefer AWS, GCP, or Azure?
Aaron leans toward AWS — it almost always produces the most value for applications. AI models can be a somewhat different story depending on size. He's used all three extensively.
Why does Aaron prefer AWS?

AWS almost always produces the most value for applications, in Aaron's experience. That said, he's used GCP and Azure extensively too — and notes that AI models can be a different story depending on size.
React, Vue, or Angular — which does Aaron prefer?

It depends on the problem. Aaron doesn't default to React for everything (though he did use it for this portfolio). He's comfortable in React, Vue, and Angular, plus Ruby on Rails, React Native, Qt, and Kotlin.
Does Aaron always use React?
No — Aaron picks the framework that fits the problem. He's comfortable in React, Vue, Angular, Ruby on Rails, React Native, Qt, and Kotlin, among others.
What IDE does Aaron use?
Lately Aaron's been using Cursor — when he uses an IDE at all. Sometimes it's just pure Claude Code. He prefers Zed as an editor but finds its AI capabilities lacking by comparison.
Does Aaron use AI coding tools?
Yes — Aaron's been using Cursor and Claude Code. He prefers Zed as a pure editor but finds its AI capabilities lacking compared to the alternatives.
TypeScript or JavaScript?

Depends on the problem. TypeScript shines in high-stakes finance, regulated industries, and higher-risk security scenarios. It's often overkill for simple CRUD apps and can waste a lot of time there. Aaron stays fluent in both.
Does Aaron like TypeScript?
Aaron finds TypeScript great for high-stakes finance, regulated industries, and security-sensitive work — but overkill for simple CRUD. He stays up-to-speed on both TS and JS and picks per problem.
How many engineers has Aaron managed?
Aaron has managed up to 10 engineers at peak.
Has Aaron led a team?
Yes — Aaron has been Technical Lead and Lead Software Development Engineer in multiple roles, and has managed up to 10 engineers at peak.
What's the biggest user base Aaron's code has served?
About 500,000 payrolled employees — for one of the largest logistics and shipping companies in the world, while Aaron was consulting at SPARQ.
What scale has Aaron worked at?
Aaron led a payroll system overhaul at SPARQ serving 500,000+ employees for a global logistics leader — that's the largest user base his code has served.
Did Aaron go to bootcamp?
Yes — Aaron attended Epicodus. It confirmed he was on the right track coding-wise and was tremendously helpful in teaching him how to navigate job seeking in the industry.
What's Epicodus?
Epicodus is the coding bootcamp Aaron attended. He found it tremendously helpful — especially its practical guidance on job seeking in the industry.
How does Aaron keep his skills current?

Aaron takes courses for cloud architecture certifications and refreshers, but mostly learns by building projects — doing, trying, and bouncing ideas off others. He finds that approach the best way to absorb difficult concepts.
How does Aaron learn new tech?
Mostly by doing. Aaron takes courses for certifications but prefers learning through projects and conversations — trying things, bouncing ideas off others, and shipping.
Has Aaron spoken at conferences?

Yes — Aaron led a 'Path to SDET' event at SPARQ, pointing aspiring QA folks toward a good path for learning test automation. He also spoke at SPARQ's Global Culture event and regularly participates in local meetups in Portland.
Does Aaron speak publicly?
Yes — Aaron led the 'Path to SDET' event at SPARQ, spoke at their Global Culture event, and regularly participates in Portland meetups.
Has Aaron written any blog posts?
Aaron is just wrapping up his first series of blog posts — stay tuned!
Does Aaron have a blog?
Aaron is wrapping up his first series of blog posts now — stay tuned!
Has Aaron won any awards?
Aaron hasn't highlighted any awards or press mentions — his focus has been on shipping real systems across multiple industries.
What's a crisis Aaron has rescued?

The last 4–5 years of Aaron's career have been systems rescue work. He's become the person counted on for the most deprecated, side-of-the-road, nobody-else-could-get-it-spun-up apps that need emergent TLC. It's made him a resilient programmer and battle-scarred DevOps engineer.
What's a hard problem Aaron has solved?

Aaron designed a solution to automate old COBOL PS file flows — reliably and efficiently — while letting those COBOL systems keep running and new systems stay backward-compatible, even 'learning' new vendor data formats. More recently, he revived an assistive tech app from the brink of total loss with massive version-jumping Rails upgrades (2.6/5 → 3.4/8), negotiating with platform providers along the way.
Tell me about the Rails upgrade at Forbes AAC.

Aaron revived Forbes AAC's assistive technology app from the brink of total loss, performing last-minute, massive version-jumping Ruby on Rails upgrades from 2.6/5 to 3.4/8. Combined with soft-skills negotiation with platform providers, the result was less downtime than expected and an app that kept serving users through a full rebuild.
What's Aaron most excited to build next?

Aaron's deep into machine learning right now — custom-training open-source LLMs and working with AWS Polly, Lex, and Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT APIs. He builds AI, not just integrates it, and believes we're only scratching the surface of what's possible.
Is Aaron doing AI work?
Yes — Aaron is actively custom-training open-source LLMs and building with AWS Polly, Lex, Claude, and ChatGPT APIs. He builds AI systems, not just wires them up.
Has Aaron trained his own LLM?
Yes — Aaron custom-trains open-source LLMs. The chat you're using right now runs on a model he fine-tuned himself on his own resume data.
Does Aaron build AI or just use it?
Both — Aaron doesn't only integrate AI, he builds it. He custom-trains open-source LLMs and works across AWS AI services, Claude, and OpenAI APIs.
Is Aaron an AI/ML researcher?
Aaron's AI/ML work is applied and hands-on — shipping real systems — not academic research. He custom-trains open-source LLMs and builds with cloud AI services.
What APIs has Aaron built with for AI?
Aaron has built with AWS Polly, Amazon Lex, Anthropic Claude, and OpenAI's ChatGPT APIs, among others. He also custom-trains open-source LLMs.
